channel.title: Live Full Stack
channel.description: A daily roundup of the news: local and world news, sports, culture, and science and tech.

item.title: Sunday, November 1, 2026: Gunfire at a Fairfield Halloween store leaves one dead and six hurt
item.description:
A shooting at a Fairfield Halloween store left one dead and six hurt, and a new analysis challenges the federal list of “likely noncitizen” voters in California ahead of Tuesday’s election. Clocks fall back an hour this weekend. The Golden State Valkyries won their first WNBA title and will parade in San Francisco on Wednesday, the Warriors rest Stephen Curry against the Clippers, and NASA is asking industry how to rescue the Hubble Space Telescope.

  • Gunfire at a Fairfield Halloween store leaves one dead and six hurt (General news)
  • Analysis: 42% of names on DOJ’s “likely noncitizen” list aren’t on California’s voter rolls (General news)
  • Valkyries win the WNBA title in Game 7 for the franchise’s first championship (Sports)
  • Netflix renews “The Diplomat” for a fifth season (Culture)
  • NASA asks industry how to lift Hubble into a safer orbit (Science & tech)

item.title: Saturday, October 31, 2026: Layoffs pile up as October ends, including cuts in San Francisco
item.description:
Job cuts kept coming as October ended, including small rounds at Dropbox and Front in San Francisco. Tech companies are now among the biggest outside spenders in California’s legislative races. The Warriors evened their record with a win over the Lakers, and tonight’s sky offers Saturn and early Halloween fireballs.

  • Layoffs pile up as October ends, including cuts in San Francisco (General news)
  • Tech money makes up at least a fifth of outside spending in California legislative races (General news)
  • Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 to reach .500 (Sports)
  • Halloween night sky: Saturn and early fireballs (Science & tech)

item.title: Friday, October 30, 2026: Halloween weekend brings a coastal flood advisory and a chance of drizzle
item.description:
High tides and light rain could greet Bay Area trick-or-treaters this weekend, with a coastal flood advisory along the bay through Sunday. A CalMatters analysis finds Prop. 45 could open a door for data centers, and the Warriors host the Lakers tonight. Astronauts completed the 100th US spacewalk from the space station, and Virgin Galactic’s new space plane flew for the first time.

  • Halloween weekend brings a coastal flood advisory and a chance of drizzle (General news)
  • Could Prop. 45 open the door to more California data centers? (General news)
  • Astronauts mark the 100th US spacewalk from the space station (Science & tech)
  • New this weekend: Apple TV’s Nocturne and Dexter: Resurrection season 2 (Culture)

item.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026: Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% as two officials push for a hike
item.description:
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, but two officials wanted a hike. A federal judge refused to make California set aside 20,000 ballots, and the head of the state’s high-speed rail project resigned. San Mateo County voters weigh an $848 million college bond, Stephen Curry scored 44 in a Warriors win, and actor Patrick Stewart died at 86.

  • Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% as two officials push for a hike (General news)
  • Judge refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots (General news)
  • Measure V asks San Mateo County voters to extend an $848 million college bond (General news)
  • Patrick Stewart, Star Trek’s Captain Picard, dies at 86 (Culture)
  • Curry scores 44 as the Warriors win at Minnesota (Sports)

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026: About $164 million has flowed through Mayor Lurie’s political and charity network
item.description:
A new investigation traces about $164 million that has flowed through San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie’s political and philanthropic network. In California, most of the state’s Republican House members have not signed a pledge to seat election winners. Astronomers may have found a sixth dwarf planet, GitHub launched a tool that picks AI models for you, and the final Dune: Part Three trailer arrived.

  • About $164 million has flowed through Mayor Lurie’s political and charity network (General news)
  • Most California Republicans in Congress skip a pledge to seat election winners (General news)
  • Astronomers spot a possible new dwarf planet beyond Neptune (Science & tech)
  • Final Dune: Part Three trailer lands ahead of a Dec. 18 release (Culture)

item.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
item.description:
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about a quarter of its workforce, and high tides flooded low-lying roads around the bay, with more expected this week. California’s ballot deadlines are closing in, and a river otter turned up on the San Mateo coast for the first time in more than a century. The Warriors got their first win, and Star Trek actor Walter Koenig died at 90.

  • Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees (General news)
  • King tides flood bayside roads, with more high water due this week (General news)
  • A river otter returns to the San Mateo coast after more than 100 years (General news)
  • Warriors earn their first win, routing Denver 134–114 (Sports)
  • Star Trek’s Walter Koenig, who played Chekov, dies at 90 (Culture)

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026: San Mateo County urges early storm prep as a strong El Niño grows likely
item.description:
San Mateo County is urging residents to get ready now for what could be a strong El Niño winter. The 49ers lost their first game of the season in Atlanta, and the Warriors try again for their first win tonight in Denver. Tonight’s Hunter’s Moon is the best full moon of the fall to catch rising.

  • San Mateo County urges early storm prep as a strong El Niño grows likely (General news)
  • 49ers’ unbeaten run ends with a 29–20 loss in Atlanta (Sports)
  • October’s Hunter’s Moon peaks overnight (Science & tech)
  • New this week: The Mob on Hulu and Netflix’s Minimum Wage (Culture)

item.title: Sunday, October 25, 2026: US pulls diplomats from Middle East posts after warning of Iranian plots
item.description:
The US pulled diplomats and their families from several Middle East posts after an intelligence warning about Iranian plots. Closer to home, seven more San Mateo County vote centers opened, and Californians are weighing about $44 billion in bond measures. The 49ers welcome back Christian Kirk for today’s game, Clayface led Friday’s box office, and the late-October sky offers a full moon and Halloween fireballs.

  • US pulls diplomats from Middle East posts after warning of Iranian plots (General news)
  • Seven more San Mateo County vote centers open ahead of Nov. 3 (General news)
  • 49ers activate Christian Kirk as Evans and Samuel sit out (Sports)
  • California voters face about $44 billion in bond measures (General news)
  • Clayface leads Friday’s box office as a Nathan Fielder documentary expands (Culture)

item.title: Saturday, October 24, 2026: Tankers burn near Hormuz as US–Iran tensions rise before the midterms
item.description:
Bay Area voters are weighing a regional transit tax that decides the future of BART and Caltrain service, and San Francisco declared a local emergency to get ready for a wet El Niño winter. Abroad, burning tankers near the Strait of Hormuz kept US–Iran tensions high. The unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta, DC’s Clayface opens in theaters, and NASA laid out a faster path back to the Moon.

  • Tankers burn near Hormuz as US–Iran tensions rise before the midterms (General news)
  • Bay Area transit tax on the Nov. 3 ballot would decide BART and Caltrain cuts (General news)
  • Unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta short on healthy receivers (Sports)
  • NASA lays out a faster Artemis plan aimed at a 2028 Moon landing (Science & tech)
  • DC’s Clayface opens with $3.5 million in previews and strong reviews (Culture)

item.title: Friday, October 2, 2026: Voters will decide a $7.5 billion science research bond in 2028
item.description:
Newsom’s last signature as governor puts a $7.5 billion science research bond before voters in 2028, and the Pentagon is creating a new command for autonomous weapons. SpaceX’s Crew-13 reached the space station Thursday night, and Steve Kerr is rebuilding the Warriors’ offense around five shooters. In theaters this weekend, Verity is expected to beat Tom Cruise’s Digger, and Miranda Lambert releases a country-disco album.

  • Voters will decide a $7.5 billion science research bond in 2028 (General news)
  • Crew-13 docks at the space station (Science & tech)
  • Pentagon creates a new command for autonomous drones and robots (General news)
  • New this weekend: Verity and Digger hit theaters, plus Miranda Lambert’s disco turn (Culture)
  • Kerr installs a five-out offense at Warriors camp (Sports)

item.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026: Newsom wraps up his last bill-signing season as governor
item.description:
Gov. Gavin Newsom closed out his final bill-signing season with new limits on addictive social media features for teens, a child marriage ban and a slate of AI rules, while forecasters say Bay Area warmth could last into mid-October. Nationally, the Supreme Court let third-country deportations continue and the Pentagon confirmed the last U.S. troops have left Iraq. The unbeaten 49ers get ready for Denver, and SpaceX’s Crew-13 is set to launch this morning.

  • Newsom wraps up his last bill-signing season as governor (General news)
  • Supreme Court lets third-country deportations resume for now (General news)
  • Last U.S. troops leave Iraq, ending the anti-ISIS mission there (General news)
  • SpaceX Crew-13 set to launch to the space station this morning (Science & tech)
  • Today in sports: unbeaten 49ers turn to Denver (Sports)
